title: Age limits, youngsters in the parade, pleasure fund and death fund
summary: Members are 18 to 65; the Jolly Boys are for pleasure, with separate pleasure and death accounts.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: How old does a man have to be to join the Jolly Boy? 18 to 65. 18 to 65. Once you hit 65 you can't join? No, after you get over that. Well we got some of them in there over that.

But that's the rule. We have a lot of youngsters. Around 8, 7, 15, 16 years old, 13 years old, they parade with us. We don't charge them nothing to parade. All they do is just buy their parents, buy their clothes and they... We'll have maybe eight to ten youngsters, brothers like that. All up. They don't charge them nothing to parade. Because you can't join the club, they do young, but we just let them come out. Now this fellow Madelea, he asked me Sunday about the... It's his boy. I think his boy was out with us Sunday, he was. When he's tall, he's a little, but he's young. He said, what we gonna do about his boy? I said, buy his clothes and they don't even come out. That's all. I'm gonna have to take it away. What's the purpose of the Jolly Bunch? Well, what you say, Jolly Boys. Just a lot of lively fellas. That's what a name, Gumpo. They like sport. They like to eat and drink. And of course, we'll name this the Jolly Bunch. But when they get together, they all like to drink and eat. So as they meetin', after meetin', they'll have sandwiches and beer and whatever they wanna drink. How much money they got? If they got fifteen dollars, they drink up to fifteen dollars. You see? But now it's just a little different. Now because we don't take care of the sick. We're not an aide. We're a pleasure. We don't aid. Now, two lands are an aide. But the Jolly one's not an aide. It's just strictly a pleasure. We used to give four enterprises a year. We spent seventy-five, eighty, ninety dollars every three months, eat and drink. Well, that's what the most of the people's in there for. You wanna tell the truth, you know, drinking. They don't have to buy it. That's all. That comes out of the treasure. But we have a debt fund. We have to give those people what we promised them. And we have two bank accounts. One for pleasure, one for death. You can't use that death fund unless somebody dies. But that pleasure, you can do what you want. Well, if you break it, it's all right. So now they're trying to build their pleasure fund back up. And last, the young people last, they had a picnic. That picnic cost us $5,500. And not without taxing the members. And these things can't be done without tax. You just can't do it on this dude. And thirty-five percent of your dues go to the debt fund. One of these guys right there at the table, every time a dollar goes across, a dollar and ten cents go across there, he gets thirty-five cents out of that. Well that don't be taxed at all. We got two treasures. One strictly for the debt fund, and one for the pleasure. Because if we didn't do that, some guy would jump up and make a move that we should have so and give so and so and so. When I have to take all of my debt fund, now we're going to lose a member. Now we're trying to get away from that tax, you see, for membership. A member died when we were trying to get away from that tax. If we can build up enough in our debt fund, we won't have to do that. So we're going to refine it. No.
